ID: 55051

What is your role and surroundings?

Our Faurecia Mercedes-Benz Sales Unit is looking for you as a VIE Sales Engineer m/f for our Customer’s Office in Böblingen (Stuttgart area), Germany.

The VIE Sales Engineer is working with, and learning from the Program Sales Lead MBAG within Faurecia Automotive Seating. He/she reports to the Sales Manager and will work on different commercial management objectives during the period of employment.

The VIE will start with an orientation phase supporting the Sales Department. After sales fundamentals on-boarding is complete, based on skill and interest- the candidate will manage specific Sales tasks in his/her own responsibility – with close support of his/her N+1.

An intercultural background, including German language and cultural proximity would be a plus to support the Program Team in exchange and alignment with our central functions. On top we support your development and deep understanding of German culture and language during the mission. With this combination, we will create an opportunity for a further career path potentially within Faurecia. Pending on interest and development of the candidate, Faurecia tries an extension of the 1st mission by additional 12 month on-site at our Böblingen Customer’s Office with different Sales Experiences in either another project or scope in order to ensure full development of a potential Sales Engineer within Faurecia.

What will be your main missions?

- In coordination with the Sales Manager and the sales engineers, preparation of internal documentation, presentations as well as conducting negotiations with the Customer (MBAG)
- Support in reporting and monitoring
- Ensure permanent contact with various internal and external departments incl. our Plants and Core Team colleagues, resilient and strongly driven to face complexity
- Coordinate the implementation of technical and commercial offers
- Ensure that the evolution of permanent parts pricing in line with the Divisions budget
- Support in budget & volume planning

The mission will last 12 months (with preferable option to extend to 24 months).

What you need to join us?

- Master’s degree in Engineering and/or Economics. - Commercial negotiation & orientation is a plus
- Passion for automotive à commercials & negotiation as a wished career path
- English language is mandatory as you will be speaking with people from all over the world.
- Microsoft® Excel® acumen

Who are we looking for?

- International mindset and strong analytical skills
- Results oriented and very driven, with strong written and oral communications skills
- A proactive approach to work and optimist energy;
- Good interpersonal skills.

What will this role offer you?

- You will work within an international Sales team full of energy;
- You will work on challenges
- You will find a strong emphasis on talent development and abundant opportunities for growth;
- You will grow professionally, polyvalence and autonomy will be part of your daily work;
- A powerful VIE community spirit within Forvians.

jobs.occupation: Space Safety System Engineer (m/f/d) (Ingenieur/in - Systems Engineering)
jobs.description:
Your Tasks

- Contribute to the development of In-Orbit Servicing (IOS), Active Debris Removal (ADR), Rendezvous and Docking (RVD) missions and related applications
- Analyse customer, mission and system requirements, including functional analyses, specification tree development and identification of required design adaptations
- Perform requirements engineering activities, including the decomposition and allocation of requirements to platform and subsystem level using DOORS and Polarion
- Monitor compliance with system requirements, coordinate with the Project Chief Engineer and Project Management, and initiate appropriate corrective actions where necessary.
- Support trade-off analyses and contribute to the definition of mission and system architectures.
- Contribute to the design and development of space systems, covering mission design, system architecture, subsystem definition and technical specifications.
- Manage and maintain system-level engineering budgets, including performance, mass, power and data budgets.
- Support interface management and budget management within the assigned engineering domain
- Contribute to the development and maintenance of the system Concept of Operations (CONOPS)
- Coordinate technical activities across subsystems, including impact assessments resulting from requirement changes, under the guidance of the Project Chief Engineer
- Support the technical coordination and management of subcontractors
- Provide direct engineering support and technical reporting to the Project Chief Engineer
- Support key system engineering reviews, including PDR, CDR and verification planning activities
- Assist in the implementation of approved design changes and the management of engineering deviations and non-conformances, including RFWs, RFDs and NCRs
- Contribute to system and subsystem verification activities, including the definition of test plans, test procedures and the evaluation of test results
- Prepare and maintain project documentation by coordinating technical inputs and documenting assigned work packages
- Support the preparation of technical proposals and bids for ADR and in-orbit servicing missions
Your Qualifications

- You hold a degree in Aerospace Engineering or a comparable technical field and have gained several years of experience in Systems Engineering, ideally within the space industry or another high-tech environment
- You are familiar with the full engineering lifecycle, from requirements analysis and specification development to defining system architectures and managing interfaces across complex projects
- You enjoy working in multidisciplinary teams and are confident communicating with a wide range of technical stakeholders
- A structured, solution-oriented approach, combined with creativity and a collaborative mindset, enables you to successfully tackle complex engineering challenges
- Experience in Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC) and Rendezvous & Docking (RvD) would be a valuable asset. Fluency in English is essential, while German language skills are considered a plus

jobs.occupation: Project Manager Science, Exploration and Space Safety (m/f/d) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description:
Your Tasks

The Directorate of Predevelopment, Proposals and Space System Studies is a strategic cornerstone of the company’s project pipeline. It drives the early shaping of future space missions by translating customer requirements into technically sound and competitive concepts. Within this directorate, the Department of Science, Exploration and Space Safety Missions focuses on the conceptualisation and maturation of missions related to astrophysics, planetary science, robotic solar system exploration, space safety, planetary defence, space weather, in-orbit servicing, in-space logistics and debris mitigation. By bridging scientific ambition with engineering feasibility, the department plays a key role in securing the OHB’s leadership in future international space programs.

As an experienced and committed Project Manager (m/f/d), you will be responsible for the successful implementation of exciting and complex proposals and projects in the domains of science and space safety in Phases 0/A and B1. You will lead interdisciplinary project teams, ensuring efficient collaboration and optimal performance. You will play a key role in the planning, coordination and management of projects to ensure that they are completed on time, cost-effectively and to the highest quality.

Your Tasks

- Responsible for the project management for proposals and projects in Phases 0/A/B1. Be accountable for the cost, schedule and performance of studies or projects.
- Support the preparation and implementation of mission and system proposals.
- Analysis, definition and agreement of the requirements with the project team and the customer(s). Lead negotiation with customers, potential partners and suppliers.
- Strengthen our relationships with clients, and act as a liaison with key stakeholders in client organisations.
Your Qualifications

- Successful completion of studies in aerospace, engineering, or a related field, demonstrating your expertise in the subject matter.
- Significant projessional experince as project manager for Phase 0/A/B1 projects, preferrably in the domains science, exploration and/or space safety. Significant experience in dealing with ESA as a customer.
- Knowledge of space projects, including systems and operations.
- Proven expertise in crafting compelling proposals
- Passion and knowledge in the space field are not just desirable but form the foundation of our collective success.
Exceptional communication and negotiation skills.
- Strong result orientation, operational efficiency and ability to reach pragmatic and timely decisions.
- Proficiency in English. Fluency in German is an advantage.

jobs.occupation: System Engineering Manager Space System Studies (m/f/d) (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
Your Tasks

As a System Engineering Manager Predevelopment, you will take a leading role in shaping the early phases of cutting‑edge satellite missions. In this position, you will drive system engineering activities during Phase A/B1, provide technical leadership across specialist teams and subcontractors, and steer the definition of the mission and system architecture. You will be responsible to establish the technical, programmatic, and schedule foundations that ensure mission success throughout the entire development lifecycle.

Tasks:

- Lead System Engineer for the Phase A/B1 study.
- Coordinate and oversee technical contributions from specialist engineering departments and subcontractors, ensuring coherence and quality.
- Perform and guide trade-offs and high-level analyses to shape the mission and system architecture.
- Lead the mission and system design, including deriving, validating, and maintaining requirements from mission to satellite down to subsystem level.
- Establish the satellite development approach to secure the targeted Technology Readiness Level (TRL) by the end of Phase B1.
- Contribute to the definition of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) for phases B2, C/D, and E1 through in‑orbit commissioning.
- Support the development and consolidation of the programme plan for phases B2, C/D, and E1 up to in-orbit calibration and validation.
- Support and review the establishment of a project implementation schedule for the platform aligned with overall programme planning.
- Analyse and assess cost drivers, contributing to cost modelling and optimization strategies.
- Identify, evaluate, and help manage technical and programmatic risks related to cost, schedule, and technical feasibility.
- Plan and implement risk mitigation measures for the platform.
Your Qualifications

Minimum:

- Master-level degree in aerospace engineering with a focus on space systems
- Minimum 8 years of industry experience in space system engineering or satellite development.
- Strong competencies in space mission design, satellite systems engineering, and spacecraft subsystem design.
- Experience in requirements engineering for spacecraft subsystems and preparation of specifications.
- Familiarity with science, exploration, or space safety mission concepts.
- High level of flexibility and ability to work effectively in international, interdisciplinary teams.
- Strong ownership mindset, structured and proactive working approach, and strong sense of responsibility.
- Excellent communication, presentation, and documentation skills.
- Fluency in spoken and written (business) English.

Ideal:

- Significant experience working as a lead system engineer for Phase 0/A/B1 projects and proposals in industry or on institutional side.
- Hands‑on experience with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) toolchains and methodologies
- Fluency in German language is an advantage

jobs.occupation: Project Manager Earth Observation Missions (m/f/d) (Ingenieur/in - Systems Engineering)
jobs.description:
Your Tasks

- Leading the preparation and execution of Earth Observation mission and system proposals for ESA, EC, DLR, commercial customers etc.
- Leading the project team throughout the development of the project
- Organize and lead regular project meetings to plan and review the project progress
- Analyse, define and coordinate requirements with the project team and the customer(s)
- Management and co-ordination of individual project partners and subcontractors
- Be responsible for the cost, schedule and performance of studies or projects
- Leading the negotiations, strengthening our relationships with clients, and acting as a liaison to key stakeholders in client organisations
Your Qualifications

- Successful completion of a degree in aerospace, engineering or a related field that demonstrates your expertise
- At least five years of relevant practical experience, preferably in the dynamic space industry, where you have demonstrated your practical knowledge
- Knowledge of space projects, including systems and operations
- Proven experience in preparing persuasive proposals that emphasizes your ability to make effective presentations.
- A deep understanding of complicated institutional structures that will enable you to navigate our challenging environment
- Passion and knowledge in the field of space is not only desirable, but is the foundation for our mutual success. An understanding of Earth Observation remote sensing principles (optical and microwave) would be an advantage
- Experience with applicable standards (ECSS) is desirable
- Exceptional communication and negotiation skills
- Strong result orientation, operational efficiency, high sense of responsibility and ability to make pragmatic and timely decisions
- High level of flexibility, willingness to work in international teams and ability to meet tight schedules
- Proficiency in the English language
